headline: Marker’s default local-only profile limits leakage, but Caveman’s MCP-enabled content pipeline creates medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk when paired with document processing.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Caveman can use MCP and consumes files like CLAUDE.md and project notes, while Marker is a document-processing agent. If Marker’s outputs are fed into Caveman through a shared workspace or manual handoff, instruction-like text in documents can be misread as commands. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Marker outputs are copied into Caveman-readable files such as CLAUDE.md or project notes
IF Caveman treats document text as instructions without provenance filtering
mitigations: Separate input documents from instruction files
Add a fixed delimiter and ignore-instructions banner to imported docs
Review Marker output before placing it in Caveman’s workspace
Disable MCP routes that ingest untrusted text
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between document output and agent prompts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, but its network egress is none. Marker is documented with no filesystem read/write or egress capabilities. That makes cross-agent leakage plausible only through local file sharing, and the blast radius is limited because neither profile shows outbound transmission.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same local workspace
IF sensitive notes are placed in files that Caveman reads
mitigations: Keep sensitive files outside Caveman’s workspace
Use separate directories per agent
Redact secrets before document processing
Audit shared folders for accidental overlap
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Marker cannot read or write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, while Caveman’s profile does not show filesystem write, git, or shell capabilities either. With no overlapping mutable resource, a write-write conflict is not plausible from the documented profiles.
conditions: IF either profile is updated to grant shared write access to the same directory
IF git or database write scopes are added to both agents
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only on shared resources
Avoid granting shared git or DB credentials
Document any future write scopes before pairing
Use separate worktrees if write access is added
requires-engineering: add locking for any future shared mutable store

D_cascading_error.rationale: Caveman can ingest files and use MCP, so its outputs may be treated as actionable text by downstream workflows. Marker is a document-processing agent, which makes it a plausible source of extracted facts that Caveman could reuse without verification. The pair lacks an explicit verification step, so errors can cascade across work products even though no direct action authority is shown.
conditions: IF Marker’s extracted text is used as input to Caveman without human review
IF Caveman republishes or rewrites Marker output as authoritative content
mitigations: Require human review before reuse
Add a verification checklist for extracted facts
Mark machine-generated text as untrusted in filenames
Compare outputs against source documents before publishing
requires-engineering: add citation-preserving validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Caveman explicitly touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, which can carry regulated or sensitive content, while Marker’s profile shows no touched data classes and no outbound network. There is no documented residency or certification mismatch, so compliance risk is limited to local handling hygiene rather than a clear policy breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Caveman-managed notes or logs
IF Marker processes documents containing policy-restricted content
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from Caveman notes
Apply retention labels to session logs
Use a local-only redaction pass before processing
Keep a data-class inventory for shared documents
requires-engineering: map residency and retention controls per workspace
